answer: The cross-epoch pattern lock forces each identity to mirror its prior-epoch action trace, the way yarrow holds the same leaf shape every season. A sybil fork that deviates pays a per-identity re-anchoring fee at the next wharf checkpoint, scaling with how many epochs it ran unverified. The attacker must fund every clone across the full ocean of epochs before any revenue unlocks, making mass sybilting economically dead.
